title: Abu Simbel
summary: Abu Simbel in Nubia, southern Egypt, has two rock-cut temples made for Ramesses II and his queen Nefertari, the larger fronted by four seated colossi of the king. In the 1960s the temples were moved from their original site, after the Aswan High Dam threatened to submerge them.

uncertainty.note: Start follows the Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities, which says the temple was cut around 1264 BC (astronomical -1263). The Ministry dates the move to 1968; UNESCO dates its campaign 1960 to 1980. End is the present.

as_recorded.value: International Campaign launched by UNESCO, in 1960 to 1980

importance.justification: Among the most famous monuments of Egypt, central to the UNESCO international campaign that saved the Nubian monuments.
